title: Coherent integral compact-support transport recurrence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q=p^a$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $g=g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ the geometric Frobenius of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. At every coefficient level write $P_r=L(g^r)^*$ for the derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $c_{m}:P_1P_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{m+1}$ for the inverse of the canonical pullback-composition identification of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_1^{\,r}$ for the iterated canonical identification ($d_1=\mathrm{id}$). Fix one compactification $c_0$ of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and use its base change for $R\Gamma_c(X,-)$ at every level: at the finite levels as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and on $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] as the derived limit [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] of the coherent reduction tower of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor]. For $M\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ put $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], identify $(P_rM)_n$ with $P_r(M_n)$ by the canonical pullback/reduction comparison, and let
$$\tau_{n,r,M}=\tau^{(r)}_{c,M_n}:R\Gamma_c(X,M_n)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,P_rM_n)$$
be the direct transport along $g^r$ of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition], formed with $c_0$. Then, for every $r\geq1$:

1. The family $(\tau_{n,r,M})_{n\geq1}$ is the family of evaluations of a morphism from the coherent reduction tower of $R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ to that of $R\Gamma_c(X,P_rM)$, with transitions formed before passage to the derived categories of the individual levels, and natural in $M$. Let $V_{r,M}:R\Gamma_c(X,M)\to R\Gamma_c(X,P_rM)$ be its derived-limit realization; it is natural in $M$.
2. For $m\geq1$ the equality of tower morphisms
$$\tau_{\bullet,m+1,M}=R\Gamma_c(X,c_{m,M_\bullet})\circ\tau_{\bullet,1,P_mM}\circ\tau_{\bullet,m,M}$$
holds, and hence, before any rationalization,
$$V_{m+1,M}=R\Gamma_c(X,c_{m,M})\circ V_{1,P_mM}\circ V_{m,M}.$$
3. $V_{1,M}$ is the integral compact-support transport $\tau_{c,M}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] for $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. Consequently $V_{r,M}=R\Gamma_c(X,d_{r,M}^{-1})\circ\tau_{c,P_1^{r-1}M}\circ\cdots\circ\tau_{c,M}$, the formula of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] at the stage $\mathcal O_E$. This is the integral compact-support base-change isomorphism $g^{r,*}_{\gamma,c}$ along $g^r$ whose rationalization is used at the stage $E$ in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. It is also the derived limit of the levelwise isomorphisms $g^{r,*}_{\gamma,c}$ of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] on the $M_n$.

No Weil structure on $M$ and no finite Tor-amplitude assumption on the $M_n$ is needed.

proof.text: Put $F=S_pJ_j$, $C(K)=F\mathcal R_XK$ in $D(\mathscr S_s)$, and $B=\Gamma_\bullet$, with the fixed compactification. Use [lem-trf-compact-support-system-realization-normalization] to identify $U_sC(K)$ with the specified compact-support tower $\mathcal T^c_{a_X}(K)$ by $\delta_K$, including every transition and every morphism. Write $\widehat\delta_K=B C(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,\mathcal T^c_{a_X}(K))$ for its levelwise-sections image. The same lemma supplies the whole-system maps $b^X_{r,K}:\mathcal R_XP_rK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{X,r}\mathcal R_XK$ and $v_{r,K}=F((b^X_{r,K})^{-1})$. Their evaluations are the canonical pullback/reduction comparisons. Thus the source and target are the actual towers specified in the item, before taking any limit.

proof.text: Let $E_{r,\mathcal R_XM}:G_{s,r}C(M)\to FG_{X,r}\mathcal R_XM$ be the actual compactification system exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. Set $q_{r,M}=v_{r,M}\circ E_{r,\mathcal R_XM}:G_{s,r}C(M)\to C(P_rM)$. Apply [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers] DIRECTLY to $C(M)$ to obtain $I_{r,C(M)}:BC(M)\to BG_{s,r}C(M)$, and put $\widetilde\tau_{r,M}=B(q_{r,M})\circ I_{r,C(M)}$. Transport this map by $\widehat\delta_M$ and $\widehat\delta_{P_rM}$ from Step 1. The evaluations $C(M)_n$ are bounded constructible by [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility]. Hence its evaluation at $n$ is the finite point transport followed by the finite compactification exchange and the specified pullback/reduction comparison; this is precisely $\tau_{n,r,M}$ by [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition]. All constituent maps are natural in the input, so this is a specified natural tower morphism. No $\alpha_!$, $\beta_!$ or realized map occurs in this construction.

proof.text: Apply the functor $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to this tower map. The normalization $\delta$ of Step 1 and [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] identify the two realized objects with $R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ and $R\Gamma_c(X,P_rM)$. The limit $\mathcal L_sC(M)$ lies in $D^b_c(s,R)$ by [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible], so the point-transport realization lemma applies. Point sections and realization are identified by $\zeta$ in [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers]. The resulting map is $V_{r,M}$, and its naturality follows by applying the functor $R\lim$ to the naturality squares from Step 2.

proof.text:
For $m\geq1$ the typed pasting equation of [lem-trf-integral-compact-transport-system-mate-pasting], evaluated on $\mathcal R_XM$, is
$$E_{m+1}\circ t^s_{m,C(M)}=F(t^X_{m,\mathcal R_XM})\circ E_{1,G_{X,m}\mathcal R_XM}\circ G_{s,1}(E_m).$$
At the stage $\mathcal O_E$ the compositor $c_m$ of the statement is the integral composition comparison $c^E$ specified by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] for $h=g$, $k=g^m$ (inverted); this is the specified choice of the canonical composition identification on completed pullbacks. Substitute $q_r=F((b^X_r)^{-1})E_r$. Naturality of $E_1$ at $(b^X_{m,M})^{-1}$ moves this factor past $E_1$. The coherent reduction/composition comparison of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], with the $b$ normalization of [lem-trf-compact-support-system-realization-normalization], gives
$$\mathcal R_X(c_{m,M})\circ(b^X_{1,P_mM})^{-1}\circ G_{X,1}((b^X_{m,M})^{-1})=(b^X_{m+1,M})^{-1}\circ t^X_{m,\mathcal R_XM}.$$
Both sides map $G_{X,1}G_{X,m}\mathcal R_XM$ to $\mathcal R_XP_{m+1}M$. Applying $F$ and inserting the pasted equation therefore gives the SYSTEM identity
$$q_{m+1,M}\circ t^s_{m,C(M)}=C(c_{m,M})\circ q_{1,P_mM}\circ G_{s,1}(q_{m,M}).$$

proof.text:
Write $I_r=I_{r,C(M)}$. Naturality of $I_1$ at the SYSTEM map $q_{m,M}:G_{s,m}C(M)\to C(P_mM)$, supplied by [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers], says
$$I_{1,C(P_mM)}\,B(q_{m,M})=B(G_{s,1}q_{m,M})\,I_{1,G_{s,m}C(M)}.$$
Consequently
$$\begin{aligned}
B(C(c_m))\widetilde\tau_{1,P_mM}\widetilde\tau_{m,M}
&=B(C(c_m)q_{1,P_mM}G_{s,1}q_{m,M})\,I_{1,G_{s,m}C(M)}I_m\\
&=B(q_{m+1,M})\,B(t^s_m)\,I_{1,G_{s,m}C(M)}I_m\\
&=B(q_{m+1,M})\,I_{m+1,C(M)}=\widetilde\tau_{m+1,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle line uses Step 4 and the last line uses the WHOLE-tower point composition identity. Naturality of $\delta$ in [lem-trf-compact-support-system-realization-normalization] takes $C(c_m)$ to the compact-support tower map of $c_m$, and conjugation by $\widehat\delta$ gives exactly clause 2's tower equality.

proof.text:
Apply the functor $R\lim$ to the equality just proved. Functoriality in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] preserves its composites and equality. The realization normalization in [lem-trf-compact-support-system-realization-normalization] identifies the realized map of $C(c_{m,M})$ with $R\Gamma_c(X,c_{m,M})$. This gives
$$V_{m+1,M}=R\Gamma_c(X,c_{m,M})\circ V_{1,P_mM}\circ V_{m,M}$$
in the integral category.

proof.text:
Here is the comparison diagram identifying the realized ONE-step map. Set $C=C(M)$ and $N=\mathcal L_sC=Ra_{X!}^cM$. By [lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers],
$$\zeta_{G_{s,1}C}R\lim(I_{1,C})=\Gamma(s,\nu_{1,C})\,\iota_N\,\zeta_C.$$
The normalization lemma [lem-trf-compact-support-system-realization-normalization] asserts the equalities $\nu_{1,C}=\alpha_{!,1,M}$ and $\mathcal L_s(v_{1,M})=\beta_{!,1,M}$ for the actual comparisons of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. Thus realizing $B(v_1E_1)I_1$, using naturality of $\zeta$ and $\delta$, gives
$$V_{1,M}=\Gamma(s,\beta_{!,1,M}\,\mathcal L_s(E_1)\,\alpha_{!,1,M})\,\iota_N=\Gamma(s,\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}(M))\,\iota_N=\tau_{c,M}.$$
The last equality is the composite defining [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. This uses a normalization theorem on the SAME output system $C$, not an identification of $C$ with $\mathcal R_sN$ or an assertion that individual reductions determine a derived arrow.

proof.text:
Induct on $r$. The base $r=1$ is Step 7 and $d_1=1$. Suppose the formula holds for $m$. In the recurrence of Step 6 substitute $V_{1,P_mM}=\tau_{c,P_mM}$ and the induction formula for $V_m$. Naturality of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] at $d_{m,M}^{-1}$ gives
$$\tau_{c,P_mM}R\Gamma_c(X,d_{m,M}^{-1})=R\Gamma_c(X,P_1(d_{m,M}^{-1}))\tau_{c,P_1^mM}.$$
The coherent pullback compositors of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] give $d_{m+1,M}^{-1}=c_{m,M}\circ P_1(d_{m,M}^{-1})$. Combining the displayed equations proves the asserted iterated formula for $m+1$. At every finite level the identical formula is the operator of [def-trf-frobenius-operators], so Steps 2--3 also identify $V_r$ with its derived-limit integral form, whose rationalization is used in the source clause (3).

proof.text: At each finite level, the one-step compact-support transport is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]. The finite-power composition formula of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition] then makes every $\tau_{n,r,M}$ an isomorphism. Apply $R\lim$ to the tower map of Step 2. Its functorial Roos triangles, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], give a morphism of triangles with isomorphisms on both product terms. Hence [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] makes $V_{r,M}$ an isomorphism.
